basket noun

also wicker basket, punnet, flower basket

classical

Traupman 277

corbis, corbis f.

noun, third declension

Other words

  • fiscina, fiscinae f. — a small basket of rushes or twigs, for fruit, cheese, olives

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fl. 41: fīcōrum (Lewis & Short); Col. 12.39.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • fiscella, fiscellae f. — a little woven basket

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Tib. 2.3.15 (Lewis & Short); Verg. E. 10.71 (Lewis & Short); Ov. F. 4.743 (Lewis & Short)

  • calathus, calathī m. — a wicker basket for flowers, fruit or wool

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. E. 2.46 (Lewis & Short); Ov. F. 4.435 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 21.23 (Lewis & Short)

    A Greek word; a hand basket made in the shape of a lily (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nunc facilis rubeā texātur fiscina virgā

    now let the pliant basket be woven of bramble twigsVerg. G. 1.266

  • dum sedet et gracilī fiscellam texit hibiscō

    while he sits and weaves a little basket of slender mallowVerg. E. 10.71

See also pick, willow, harvest.
